div.head: Hu 6
div.ab: Si quis rectum declinet uel aufugiat, persoluat uno gildo (angildum) qui eum ad dampnum illud tenuit.
Gyf hwá riht forbuge ⁊ uthleape, forgylde þæt angylde se ðe hine to ðam hearme geheold.
Si quis rectitudinem deuitans effugiat, soluat illud simpliciter (quod petitur per illam calumpniam, propter quam effugit ille) qui eum (effugere) ad illud iacture seruauit.
Gyf hwá riht forbuge ⁊ uthleape, forgylde þæt angylde se ðe hine to ðam hearme geheold.
If anyone evades the law and escapes, he who has supported him in wrongdoing shall pay the damage.
If anyone evades the law and flees, he who supported him in that injury is to pay the simple compensation.
Wenn einer Rechtserfüllung vermeidet indem er entweicht, so bezahle den einfachen Ersatz wer ihn zu dieser Schadenstiftung bei sich gehalten hat.
If anyone avoids fulfilling his legal obligation by absconding, let whoever kept him for this doing of harm pay the single compensation.
div.note: This is ambiguous: se þe hitie to þam hearme geheold. Thorpe translates: “who held him to answer for the offence”. If this means the person whose business it was to see that he came to answer the charge, it does not differ in essence from Liebermann, who compares III Edmund 3, dealing with the lord’s responsibility for the deeds of men in his service. This code is only in Latin, in Quadripartitus, but the phrase qui aliquem manutenebit et firmabit ad dampnum faciendum may be translating something very like our text. The meaning seems to be “he who by maintaining him made it possible for him to commit that injury”.
i.e. the value of the stolen goods
